title: Record Keeping, Audit and Inspection Readiness
summary: What records to keep and for how long, how the training register works, how independent audit tests the program, and how to be ready for an unannounced CBUAE inspection.

lessons.title: What to keep, and for how long
lessons.body:
## Five years, at least

Keep, in a form that can be searched:

- Customer identification and due diligence records, including the **sender and receiver**.
- Details of **every transaction**.
- Correspondence and account files.
- Risk assessments and the measures taken.
- **Suspicious transaction and activity reports** and the analysis behind them.

The period is **at least five years**, counted from the completion of the transaction, the end of the relationship, the end of a CBUAE inspection or a final court judgment, depending on the case.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: Records you can use
lessons.body:
## Organised, not just stored

Records must let the LEH **analyse data, trace transactions and reconstruct** any single transaction as evidence.

Make them available to the competent authorities **immediately on request**.

Good habits:

- One standard file layout per customer.
- Write the **reason** for every decision.
- Never alter or backdate a record. Add a dated correction instead.

lessons.title: Video: Transaction monitoring explained
lessons.body:
## Before you watch

Good records make monitoring possible. This video shows how rules and alerts are used to watch transactions, and why the evidence behind each alert must be kept.

## Look out for

- How rules create alerts
- Why every alert needs a recorded decision
- What an examiner would want to see afterwards

## After watching

Answer the short quiz to move on.

*This video is made by a third party and opens on YouTube. It is not produced by Data Mine Labs or the CBUAE, and it may describe rules from other countries. Where it differs from the CBUAE Rulebook or your own policy manual, follow those.*

lessons.title: The training register
lessons.body:
## Proof of training

The LEH keeps a **central AML/CFT training register**. For each employee it records:

- The **training history**.
- **Dates** and **durations**.
- **Assessment scores**.

This is how an LEH shows it met the 30-day onboarding rule, the annual refresher and any event-driven training. Examiners can ask for it on arrival, so keep it current.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: Independent audit
lessons.body:
## Checking the checkers

- **Internal audit** regularly audits the Compliance Officer's function. It must be independent of the functions it audits and report to the Board or Owners.
- **External auditors** perform **agreed-upon procedures** on the AML/CFT compliance function **every year**.

Findings feed back into the risk assessment and into the next round of training.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: Ready for an inspection
lessons.body:
## Unannounced visits

CBUAE examiners may arrive without notice. Be ready to show:

1. The written AML/CFT program and policies, with approval dates.
2. The latest risk assessment.
3. The training register.
4. Samples of customer files and transaction records.
5. Alert and STR/SAR logs (without disclosing the content of reports to anyone not entitled).
6. Audit reports and how findings were fixed.

Be honest, cooperate, and keep a log of what was provided.
